newsitem.title: UK: Mideast crude tankers busy, UKC slips again.
newsitem.headline: Mideast crude tankers busy, UKC slips again.

text.p: The key Middle East crude tanker zone dominated business on Thursday with several ULCCs finding employement both east and west.
The UK/continent saw aframax levels slip as barrels were fixed transatlantic while in the Mediterranean healthy enquiry ensured charter rates held.
In the Middle East Saudi charterer Vela showed its hand by taking three, possibly four ULCCs.
Shipbrokers said ULCCs stole the limelight from VLCCs looking for business although sevearal 250,000 tonners were also fixed.

Rates heading to Singapore were seen to have consolidated at W65 having moved slowly higher during the course of the week from W60. Japan destinations were able to retain W75 while western-bound tankers were commanding in the high W50s.
In the slowish UK/continent market aframaxes, already under pressure from lacklustre inter UKC chartering was knocked by Norway's Statoil fixing 350,000 tonnes of Brent to the U.S. Gulf.
"Taking that much oil out of the region amounts to four or five aframax trips so its not looking so good for 80,000 tonners," said one broker.
Those aframaxes lucky enough to find a charterer for typical cross North Sea trips saw rates further eroded to W97.5-100 from the W100-105 seen on Wednesday.
In the Mediterreanean healthy fixing was keeping aframax rates on cross Med trips in the low W120s and there was room for further gains.
"There is still some way to go before people even think about double-stemming into suezmaxes (130,000 tonners)," said one Med shipbroker.
In West Africa suezmaxes were securing in the mid to high W80s with the U.S the dominant destination. A VLCC was fixed to South Korea at W52.5.
